science-source-y7-b09-d09.title: Year 7 Science — Earth resources and water cycle (original assessment)
science-source-y7-b09-d09.coverage: Source MC with created marking guidance; ambiguous items excluded. Written responses, graphing, drawing and calculations retained in the question bank.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all natural resources of the Earth?
options: rocks, fossil fuels, sunlight, water and glass.
plants, animals, sunlight, houses and rocks.
water, soil, sunlight, rocks and fossil fuels.
bridges, soil, sunlight, trees and cars.
questions.explanation: C. Water, soil, sunlight, rocks and fossil fuels are natural resources; the other lists include manufactured objects.

questions.prompt: A renewable resource is:
options: a resource that is always being replaced naturally.
a resource that takes longer than the average human lifespan to be replaced.
sun, trees and wind only.
any resource that is natural.
questions.explanation: A. Renewable resources are replenished naturally on human timescales; sustainable use also depends on the rate of consumption.

questions.prompt: The main gases in air are:
options: carbon dioxide, oxygen, chlorine and nitrogen.
nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases.
argon, water vapour, ozone and other gases.
nitrogen, water vapour, argon, methane and other gases.
questions.explanation: B is the intended best list. Nitrogen and oxygen dominate air, with argon, carbon dioxide and other trace gases.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the Sun?
options: plants use sunlight to produce food.
it warms the Earth’s atmosphere.
it is a renewable resource.
all of the above.
questions.explanation: D. Sunlight supports photosynthesis, warms Earth and is treated as renewable on human timescales.

questions.prompt: Condensation is:
options: the process of liquid becoming gas.
the process of gas becoming solid.
the process of gas becoming liquid.
the process of solid becoming gas.
questions.explanation: C. Condensation is gas changing to liquid.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all renewable energy sources?
options: biomass, solar, hydroelectricity, wind.
wind, nuclear, solar, hydroelectricity.
geothermal, wind, tidal, coal.
nuclear, biomass, geothermal, wave.
questions.explanation: A. Biomass, sunlight, hydroelectricity and wind are renewable sources when appropriately managed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the water cycle?
options: the Sun’s energy drives the water cycle.
the water can be in any of the three phases.
it is the natural process of recycling water.
all of the above.
questions.explanation: D. Solar energy drives evaporation, water changes phase, and water is recycled naturally.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not associated with the water cycle?
options: the evaporation of water from a liquid to gas state.
the deposition of sediments.
the transpiration of water from plants.
the percolation of water into the soil.
questions.explanation: B. Sediment deposition is not itself a water-cycle phase-change or water-transport process, though moving water can carry and deposit sediment.

science-source-y7-b09-d10.title: Year 7 Science — Earth, Moon and space (original assessment)
science-source-y7-b09-d10.coverage: Source MC with created marking guidance; ambiguous items excluded. Written responses, graphing, drawing and calculations retained in the question bank.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all planets?
options: Mars, Earth, Pluto, Leo, Venus.
Neptune, Uranus, Mars, Jupiter.
Scorpio, Pluto, Neptune, Saturn, Sagittarius.
Gemini, Cancer, Virgo, Pisces, Taurus.
questions.explanation: B. Neptune, Uranus, Mars and Jupiter are planets; Pluto is a dwarf planet and zodiac constellations are not planets.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true?
options: different constellations can be seen in different positions at different times of the year.
different cultures have developed different stories about the same constellations .
Some constellations are only visible in the southern hemisphere and some in the northern hemisphere.
all the statements are true.
questions.explanation: D. All three statements are broadly true; visibility depends on latitude and season.

questions.prompt: Gravity is affected by:
options: mass and distance.
mass only.
distance only.
mass, distance and light.
questions.explanation: A. Gravitational attraction depends on masses and separation distance.

questions.prompt: In a solar eclipse which of the following occurs?
options: Earth blocks the sunlight from the Moon.
Moon blocks the sunlight from the Earth.
Sun gets in the way of us seeing the Moon.
a comet blocks the Sun.
questions.explanation: B. The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, blocking sunlight from part of Earth.

questions.prompt: In the phases of the moon a new moon appears as:
options: a complete circle in the night sky.
a half of the moon visible in the night sky.
nothing visible in the night sky.
almost all the moon visible in the night sky.
questions.explanation: C is the intended best answer: the sunlit face points away from Earth, so the Moon is normally not visible. New moon is near the Sun in the daytime sky, rather than appearing as an unlit object all night.

questions.prompt: Earth has 4 seasons because:
options: it spins on its axis.
it would be boring to have the same climate all year.
of its orbit around the Sun.
of the tilt of the axis.
questions.explanation: D. Axial tilt, together with Earth’s revolution, changes illumination and day length through the year.

questions.prompt: Every four years we have a leap year because?
options: it makes it interesting for people born on the 29th February.
the earth is orbiting the Sun faster every four years.
the Earth is orbiting the Sun slower every four years.
it takes 365 ¼ days for the Earth to go around the Sun but you cannot have a ¼ day on a calendar.
questions.explanation: D is the simplified intention: an orbital year is about 365.24 days. Leap days account for the fraction, with century exceptions in the Gregorian calendar.

questions.prompt: Daylight hours are longest in summer and shortest in winter. An equinox is when there is equal amount of daylight hours as night hours. When would this occur?
options: autumn only.
autumn and spring.
spring only.
summer and winter.
questions.explanation: B. Equinoxes occur in autumn and spring.

science-source-y7-b09-d11.title: Year 7 Science — Chemistry and investigating science (original assessment)
science-source-y7-b09-d11.coverage: Source MC with created marking guidance; ambiguous items excluded. Written responses, graphing, drawing and calculations retained in the question bank.

questions.prompt: Which of the following correctly describes distillation?
options: a method of separation where particles of liquid, solid or gas stick to the outside surface of a solid.
a process that uses evaporation and condensation to separate solids from liquids or liquids from liquids, enabling the recovery of both.
a process that uses heat to make a liquid solvent change state to a gas, and leave behind the solute it has dissolved.
separation of solids or liquids from a liquid or gas by using a barrier with holes smaller than particles being separated.
questions.explanation: B. Distillation uses vaporisation and condensation to recover a solvent and separate components by volatility.

questions.prompt: Fast evaporation results in:
options: small crystals.
no crystals.
large crystals.
small or no crystals.
questions.explanation: D. Rapid evaporation generally favours smaller crystals or can prevent substantial crystal growth; outcome depends on conditions.

questions.prompt: In an experiment an independent variable is the one:
options: you change.
you measure.
you keep the same.
you observe.
questions.explanation: A. The independent variable is deliberately changed.

questions.prompt: Which separation technique would be useful in determining the colours a black marker is composed of?
options: filtration.
chromatography.
distillation.
absorption.
questions.explanation: B. Paper chromatography can separate the dyes in black ink (using an appropriate solvent).

questions.prompt: Which of the following are all physical properties:
options: state, colour, freezing point, reaction with oxygen.
colour, melting point, flammability, state.
density, hardness, colour, state.
reaction rate, freezing point, state, colour.
questions.explanation: C. Density, hardness, colour and state are physical properties; oxygen reaction and flammability are chemical properties.

questions.prompt: Which of the following explains why gases can be compressed?
options: particles in a gas are spread far apart.
there are no bonds between gas particles.
particles in a gas move quicker when heated.
particles in a gas are close together.
questions.explanation: A. Large spaces between gas particles allow the volume to decrease under pressure.

questions.prompt: A quantitative observation involves:
options: just watching.
words.
numbers.
diagrams.
questions.explanation: C. Quantitative observations use numbers and measurements.

questions.prompt: Which of the following describes a hypothesis?
options: what you plan to do.
an educated guess at what might happen.
a list of all the equipment.
a list of what you need to do.
questions.explanation: B is the closest option. A scientific hypothesis is a testable proposed explanation or prediction informed by evidence, more than an arbitrary guess.

questions.prompt: Changing state from gas to liquid is called:
options: boiling.
melting.
condensation.
sublimation.
questions.explanation: C. Gas changing to liquid is condensation.
